citations.desc: Attending veterinarian and adequate veterinary care (dealers and exhibitors).
citations.narrative:
There is one expired container of silver sulfadiazine cream (expiration date of 02/2026) on a shelf in the pharmacy area.
The facility representative disposed of the container when found during inspection.
The use of expired medications is not considered to be a safe or appropriate method to prevent, control, diagnose, and
treat diseases and injuries because expired drugs may be ineffective or produce other undesired effects. Animals may
experience discomfort or distress due to unrelieved symptoms or unexpected side effects from the use of expired
medication. The program for providing adequate veterinary care shall include the use of appropriate methods to prevent,
control, diagnose, and treat diseases and injuries. This includes establishing and following procedures to ensure that
medications are removed when expired and cannot be administered to animals.
CORRECTED DURING THE TIME OF THIS INSPECTION ON 07/09/2026

citations.desc: Environment enhancement to promote psychological well-being.
citations.narrative:
Two adult female ostriches and one adult male ostrich exhibit varying degrees of baldness on the hindquarters, and the
inspector and facility representative witnessed a very brief interaction where all three birds were each pecking on the
hindquarters of a different ostrich. Although the witnessed pecking was not prolonged or vicious and the plucked skin of
the birds did not appear red or irritated in appearance, the area of missing feathers was as much as ~50% of the hips and
rear, lower abdomen on the females; the remaining feathers appeared greasy or clumped and unkempt. When asked
about this, the facility representative stated that the attending veterinarian visited about 2 weeks prior and was looking into
the matter, but no one had seen any of the feather picking between the birds until the day of the inspection. The avian
environment enhancement plan lists species-specific daily enrichments for the other bird species at the zoo, but does not
specify enrichment for the ostriches. Keeper records show limited species-specific enrichment performed and the most
frequent enrichment offered was water hosing from the keeper and a mud wallow.
Ostriches are desert or semi-desert species that do not normally wallow in mud, but do dust-bathe to absorb excess oil
from their feathers and aid in temperature regulation and parasite removal. Failure to provide adequate and appropriate
enrichment to birds that encourages non-injurious, natural behaviors can cause boredom and distress or even illness and
incompatibility. The facility must ensure that the physical environment in the primary enclosures is enriched by materials
or activities that would provide the birds with the means to express non-injurious, species-typical activities. Species
differences should be considered when determining the type or methods of enrichment and be approved by the Attending
Veterinarian.
TO BE CORRECTED BY 07/21/2026
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with a facility representative.
